author_note: Written from the brief alone as plain spoken-style conversations with one deliberate property per reply, good replies kept flawless and bad replies flawed only in the named way.

Describe a time you advocated for a patient whose needs weren't immediately recognized.

On my med-surg floor I had an older man whose confusion started overnight. His wife told me it wasn't like him at all, but the team thought it was just age. I checked his vitals, saw his heart rate creeping up and his temperature rising, and called the rapid response team. They found a urinary infection heading toward sepsis and moved him to the ICU. He recovered, and his wife thanked me for listening to her.
